strengths: Well-motivated, practical problem formulation addressing lifelong learning for neural VRP solvers with distributional and scale shifts, more general than prior work
Technically sound approach with clear justification for design choices (CaEW for low-confidence decisions, reverse KLD for mode-seeking in routing)
Exceptionally comprehensive experimental evaluation: five metrics, six task distributions, five random task orders, multiple base solvers (POMO, Omni, INViT), and both synthetic and real benchmarks
Strong and consistent empirical results substantially outperforming all baselines across all metrics (e.g., CVRP AP 0.0042 vs 0.023+ for baselines)
Thorough analysis including ablation studies, hyperparameter sensitivity, and detailed supplementary material supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily combines established techniques (experience replay, confidence weighting, reverse KLD) without introducing fundamentally new lifelong learning mechanisms
Restrictive experimental setting: assumes known task boundaries, buffers only from final epochs, limited to 6 sequential tasks, unclear scalability to longer task sequences

Confidence measure inadequately justified: variance of action distribution may reflect uncertainty among options rather than decision importance; single anecdotal example (Figure 5) provided without systematic empirical validation
Incomplete methodological analysis: batch-level buffering makes |E| scale-dependent and complicates fair comparison; no theoretical analysis of stability-plasticity tradeoff or forgetting bounds

Scalability concerns acknowledged but unresolved: authors note fixed |E| difficult to tune across scales, reservoir sampling biases buffer toward high-experience tasks, memory overhead 400MB non-trivial
Modest zero-shot generalization improvements: AG values remain large and improvements may conflate with effects of sequential diversity; improvements less dramatic than AP gains
Incomplete comparisons: dismisses Li et al. (2024) and Feng et al. (2025) without detailed empirical comparison; missing comparisons with modern continual learning methods
Post-hoc explanations: hyperparameter effects differ between CVRP/TSP with task-similarity explanation lacking depth; insufficient analysis of when/why LLR-BC succeeds

strengths: Well-motivated practical problem addressing realistic scenario of sequential task learning in VRP solvers
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with multiple task orders, metrics, and benchmark datasets
Systematic ablation studies and hyperparameter sensitivity analysis demonstrating robustness
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and rigorous metric definitions
Consistent empirical improvements across diverse evaluation metrics and base solvers
Methodologically sound design choices (variance-based confidence, reverse KLD, reservoir sampling)
weaknesses: Critical gap: Complete absence of experimental comparison with Li et al. (2024) and Feng et al. (2025), the only prior works on lifelong learning for neural VRP solvers, making claims of applicability unsupported
Limited methodological novelty: primarily combines established techniques (experience replay, confidence weighting, reverse KLD) without substantial innovation
Weak baselines: outdated EWC (2017), adapted LiBOG with unclear fairness, no comparison with concurrent lifelong learning works
Insufficient analysis of method behavior: limited insight into why method works, what knowledge transfers, or characterization of failure cases; variable performance on benchmarks unexplained
Small problem scale and limited task complexity: only 6 tasks, max 100 nodes, arbitrary task-scale assignments, unclear scalability to realistic instances

Experimental design concerns: hyperparameter selection procedure unclear, metric normalization creates interdependence between methods, buffer contains only 0.01% of experiences without investigation of sufficiency

Unresolved limitations: acknowledged buffer imbalance problem without mitigation, confidence measure (variance) not compared to alternatives, batch-level implementation conflates method with engineering details
Practical analysis incomplete: memory/computational costs not compared to baselines, scalability to larger instances and more tasks unknown

strengths: Well-motivated and practically important problem: lifelong learning for neural VRP solvers addresses a realistic gap in handling sequentially arriving tasks with diverse distributions and scales
Exceptionally thorough experimental evaluation: 5 task orders, comprehensive metrics, multiple base solvers (POMO, Omni, INViT), benchmark datasets, ablations, and hyperparameter sensitivity analysis
Strong empirical results: dramatic improvements over baselines (AP: 4.2 vs 23.5+ for CVRP) with consistent gains across all metrics and task orders
Intuitive technical approach: CaEW for identifying vulnerable decisions and DsBC using reverse KLD for decision-seeking are well-motivated for routing contexts
Excellent reproducibility: detailed appendices, hyperparameter specifications, computational cost analysis, and promise to release code
Demonstrates applicability across different base solvers and problem variants (CVRP, TSP)
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: experience replay, variance-based confidence, and reverse KLD are existing techniques; primary contribution is their combination for a new application
Missing critical baseline comparisons: no direct experimental comparison with Li et al. (2024) and Feng et al. (2025), the most relevant related works on lifelong learning for neural VRP solvers
Design choices lack rigorous justification: (1) why variance over entropy for confidence?, (2) why buffer only in final epoch?, (3) why batch-level operations?—no empirical comparisons provided
Insufficient analysis of method limits: scale sensitivity observed but not deeply explored; performance degradation with INViT explained post-hoc rather than predicted; unclear when method fails
Confidence metric not validated: Figure 5 provides anecdotal motivation but no systematic comparison of different uncertainty measures; variance choice not theoretically justified
Hyperparameter sensitivity despite claims of robustness: α shows notable performance variation (Table 3), with opposite effects on TSP vs. CVRP suggesting domain-dependent tuning requirements
Limited evaluation scope: only 6 tasks evaluated; scaling to longer sequences unclear; real benchmark results (Tables 7-8) show more variance and less dramatic improvements than synthetic tasks
Significant computational overhead: 'no more than 8 additional hours' training represents non-negligible cost despite claims of efficiency
Buffer design concerns: fixed |E| potentially problematic when task scales differ greatly (acknowledged limitation); reservoir sampling favors high-experience tasks

strengths: Well-motivated practical problem addressing realistic lifelong learning scenarios for neural VRP solvers
Thorough experimental evaluation with multiple metrics, task orders, problem types, and base solvers, demonstrating substantial empirical improvements
Clear technical approach with sound justification for component choices (CaEW confidence weighting, RKLD for mode-seeking behavior)
Model-agnostic framework successfully applied across multiple base solvers (POMO, Omni, INViT)
Excellent presentation with detailed algorithms, comprehensive appendices, and reproducibility details enabling independent verification
Addresses important gap in prior work by handling uncontrollable instance generation and arbitrary task orders
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily combines established techniques (experience replay, confidence weighting, reverse KLD) without substantial innovation in individual components

Questionable baseline adaptations: significant modifications to prior methods (e.g., removing parameter B from Feng et al.) may not represent fair comparisons; insufficient analysis of why existing lifelong learning methods fail specifically for VRP
Narrow experimental scope: only 6 similar task configurations, limited to 5 random orders, no cross-variant learning, no extreme task dissimilarity testing
Insufficient design justification: buffering only final epoch needs stronger rationale; variance-based confidence measure is simplistic; limited exploration of why choices benefit VRP specifically
Weak zero-shot generalization despite claimed improvements: AG values remain high in absolute terms (26.7-41.1) with limited analysis of what knowledge actually transfers across tasks
Inconsistent performance across base solvers: INViT results show worse forgetting metrics than fine-tuning on CVRP, contradicting applicability claims and lacking thorough investigation
Missing statistical rigor: no error bars, significance tests, or confidence intervals despite averaging over only 5 task orders
Scope limitation for top-tier venue: VRP-specific focus with unclear generalization to other combinatorial optimization problems

strengths: Addresses a practical and well-motivated problem of catastrophic forgetting in sequential VRP task learning
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with multiple metrics (AP, AF, AMF, APl, AG) specifically designed for lifelong learning assessment
Consistent and substantial empirical improvements across multiple task orders, datasets (CVRP, TSP), and base solvers (POMO, Omni, INViT)
Well-structured presentation with detailed appendices, extensive ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity analysis, and benchmark evaluations
General framework independent of specific model architecture, applicable to different neural VRP solvers
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: primarily combines three existing techniques (experience replay, confidence weighting, reverse KLD) without significant innovation in individual components

Critical design choices lack strong justification: reverse KLD shows only marginal benefits over standard KLD (ablation -KLD); confidence weighting with variance shows negligible difference vs. entropy or top-2 margin; buffering policy at final epoch is arbitrary

Experimental setup fairness concerns: prior methods (Li et al. 2025, Feng et al. 2025) were significantly adapted/modified for comparison; Restart baseline uses different setting (single-task vs. lifelong); no comparison with simpler multi-task or parameter regularization baselines

Acknowledged fundamental limitation unaddressed: fixed |E| is difficult to tune when task scales differ substantially, potentially reducing plasticity on small-scale and stability on large-scale tasks

Limited problem scope: only addresses distribution and scale variations, not other task modifications; assumes all tasks equally important with fixed training budgets; claims broader applicability than actually demonstrated

Insufficient evidence for core claims: no empirical validation that low-confidence decisions are actually 'crucial'; Figure 5 example shows decisions change but not that preservation is beneficial; zero-shot improvements may stem from diverse multi-task exposure rather than lifelong learning mechanism
Sparse buffer (0.01% of training data) with no analysis of whether capacity is sufficient or larger buffers would help; no visualization or analysis of what behaviors are actually being preserved

Experimental scope limitations: only 6 tasks, 5 random orderings; results on benchmark instances (Tables 9-10) show more variable performance with some instances favoring other methods, suggesting robustness may be lower than main results suggest

strengths: Addresses a practically important and underexplored problem: lifelong learning for neural VRP solvers with uncontrollable tasks arriving sequentially, more realistic than prior work (Li et al., Feng et al.) which assumed known order and controllable instance generation

Theoretically well-motivated design: use of reverse KLD for mode-seeking behavior preservation and variance-based confidence weighting are justified with clear intuitions for constructive routing solvers

Comprehensive and rigorous experimental evaluation: five complementary metrics (AP, AF, AMF, APl, AG) across six diverse tasks, five task orders, multiple strong baselines, two problem types, and standard benchmarks (TSPLIB, CVRPLIB)

Consistently strong empirical results: substantial improvements (AP 0.0042 vs >0.023 on CVRP; 0.0034 vs >0.014 on TSP), remarkable robustness across task orders (low std.), good stability-plasticity balance, and best zero-shot generalization
Excellent reproducibility: detailed algorithms, comprehensive hyperparameters, extensive appendices (31 pages), training protocols, memory/computational cost analysis, and promise to release code
Model-agnostic framework: demonstrated applicability across multiple base solvers (POMO, Omni, INViT) with consistent improvements
Clear presentation with effective motivation, logical organization, and well-designed figures (particularly Figure 1 illustrating the problem)
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: individual components (experience replay, reverse KLD, confidence weighting) are from prior work; contribution is primarily in their combination applied to lifelong VRP rather than introducing fundamentally new techniques

Baseline adaptation concerns: Li et al. and Feng et al. were designed for controllable instance generation; the adaptation to uncontrollable scenarios may not be equivalent to their original design, and large std. deviations (e.g., Li inter TSP 77.6±59.6) raise fairness questions

Acknowledged but unresolved limitations: fixed |E| causes reduced plasticity on small-scale tasks and reduced stability on large-scale tasks; buffer composition biased toward larger scales due to reservoir sampling; these are noted but not addressed

Incomplete mechanistic understanding: while the paper asserts low-confidence decisions are important, validation beyond intuition and one example (Figure 5) is limited; deeper analysis of what behaviors are preserved and how they transfer would strengthen the work

Task-dependent hyperparameter sensitivity: α shows opposite behavior on CVRP vs. TSP (increasing α improves CVRP but worsens TSP); explanation (TSP tasks more similar) is post-hoc and limits generality claims

Limited evaluation scope: only CVRP and TSP evaluated; generalization to other routing variants (pickup-delivery, time windows) unknown; sequence length capped at k=6; scalability to longer lifelong learning scenarios (10+, 50+ tasks) not demonstrated

Modest zero-shot generalization gains: despite improvements over baselines, AG values remain substantial (26.7 for CVRP, 41.1 for TSP normalized), indicating limited knowledge transfer compared to improvements in catastrophic forgetting mitigation

Computational and memory overhead: ~8 additional training hours with unclear baseline time; memory usage (400 MB) and scalability to larger problems not thoroughly analyzed; overhead during training is non-trivial though negligible at inference

Analysis of information preservation: only buffering final epoch means early difficult phases not captured; minimal justification for why this is sufficient or comparison with alternatives (though -EE ablation in Appendix C.3 shows it's better)
